title: Wide cross-platform discovery pass 41
summary: Personally review broad cross-platform discovery: add 33 source-backed projects and record four explicit non-promotions.
notes: Root personally performed 52 broad searches returned 292 hits and 290 distinct repository URLs across classic computers and consoles, then inspected 37 selected repository roots at pinned source revisions. Added 33 projects and recorded four explicit non-promotions. Final selected-root screening caught already-tracked xdms-rs after the late search batch; retain it as a duplicate decision, not a new project. Interceptor was re-encountered but is already tracked and was not added again. Coverage includes game disassembly/decompilation/ports, historical application and language sources, debuggers/assemblers, tape/disk/archive tools, asset conversion and preservation. Broad coverage does not claim every platform or project was exhausted. No discovery worker used and no upstream software built or executed. Ingestion findings: preserve variant-specific build requirements, implemented versus planned features, partial test coverage, host/guest CPU roles and external-tool dependencies. Resolve archived package migrations into coherent root projects before adding. Sparse or inherited READMEs need implementation and secondary documentation inspection. Static source defects (dsk2woz2 extension detection) and erroneous prose (detokenizer endian speculation) must not become verified capability/architecture facts. AI configuration files alone do not establish AI development; unnamed explicit LLM disclosures retain an empty tools list. Current catalogue was fetched at pinned main 043a303babb530ea99434176ca07f14d0291109a; local large activity history uses an older cached copy, so final live ingestion and deployment checks remain necessary. Validation caught an unsupported decompiler tool-kind label; mapped it to the existing binary-analysis taxonomy while retaining decompilation work-kind. Submission prepare alone accepted this draft, so full staged catalogue validation must remain a separate required pre-publication gate.

sources.reason: Historical tracker source archive with two differently aged source trees. Author cannot confidently identify the final version; src-q/ad.c explicitly is not the version used in AProSys.

Streams SEQ/PRG files through variable-length text replacement. The README contains the actual BASIC listing, despite the tree otherwise presenting PRG files. BASIC links can be repaired; fixed-offset machine code is not safe after length changes.

Qt waveform/block interface supports processing selections, noise/frequency controls, filtering, channel changes and TAP output. Source is substantive despite no README. WAV parser expects specific PCM/chunk layouts, not arbitrary audio formats.
TZX/TAP/CSW to PZX, PZX to WAV, and editable textual pulse/block representation. Documentation specifies TZX 1.20 and CSW 1.01/2.00; do not infer support for future revisions.
Builds a DFS SSD image from files with load/execute addresses and optional generated !BOOT. Fixed 80-track, 10-sector, 256-byte geometry is not universal Acorn disk-format support.

Archive/disk inspection, extraction and conversion with format-identification and nested-container handling. CLI and Windows GUI have different host support; format recognition is not universal read/write support.

Converts standard 35-track, 16-sector, 256-byte DSK input to WOZ2. Source-level defect: extension loop overwrites has_p and has_dot from the same character, making their conjunction false; documented ProDOS-order detection is not established as working.
Reads classic pre-OS-X resource-fork types, names and data. AppleDouble handling in inspected implementation assumes a fixed layout; do not infer full modern filesystem/container support.

Historical DOS-to-C decompiler substantially reworked with a Qt frontend and MZ/PSP loading. Memory models, arrays and recovery remain constrained; historical binaries do not establish that current source builds.

Recovers BASIC from BRUN30 QuickBASIC 3 executables, including COMMON chains and floating-evaluation-order preservation. BCOM30 /O is unsupported; multi-module binaries only recover the first module. Some constant-index arrays become scalars, changing layout.

Two-disk translation rebuild handles PRECO on Disk A and FAT12 on Disk B, with input hash checks, script/image changes and IPS output. ERC VFD is a container, not an HDM rename; emulator in-memory saves require explicit flushing.

OS-9/DECB disk tools and historical ROM/compiler sources. Microware C material explicitly needs work; optional DiskShed GUI has a separate build. It is not uniformly complete simply because several components work.
Historical debugger continuation with symbol loading, terminal adaptation and a conditional HD64180/Z180 build. Version 4.2 fixes symbol files ending exactly at a record boundary.

Assembler covers several 6800/6801/6809/6301/6309/68HC11-family modes and binary, Intel HEX, S-record and FLEX relocatable outputs. RELASMB compatibility was reverse engineered and is not an exhaustive compatibility guarantee.

Combines SNES ROM mapping, labels and emulator trace/CDL information including 65816 register-width context. Importer respects the selected mapping rather than retaining inconsistent detected offsets.

RGBDS assembly reconstruction of the USA 1 MiB MBC5 CGB-only game. Named routines and asset boundaries are present; author byte-exact and coverage totals are not independent verification. Unreferenced bytes retain unknown purpose.

Loads bitmap/TGA and width-height-prefixed 16-bit texture data, converts Saturn colors/textures, writes PNG/TGA and handles selected transparency. Sparse README is supplemented by implementation evidence.

Native SH-4 port using recovered OOT game code, PowerVR display-list translation and AICA audio. Display-list interpretation is not MIPS CPU emulation. Only gc-eu-mq-dbg input is documented, not every retail ROM.

Work-in-progress reconstruction targets the July 12 NTSC-J prototype, not all retail variants. Source includes main game and IOP-module interfaces. Hardcoded overlay addresses and unrecovered details remain.
Historical homebrew Tetris source with 68000 host code and GPU game/rendering components, continued with newer tooling. Not a commercial game decompilation.
Reusable extraction/repacking, graphics, text, compression and patch helpers. WonderSwan implementation splits 64 KiB banks and recalculates checksums; other platforms have individual constraints.
Converts indexed BMP to WonderSwan Color chunky tiles, optionally deduplicating mirrored map tiles; -4col emits monochrome planar data. Output modes must not be conflated.
Early recovered functions and overlay configuration for USA Rev 0 YLZE01. Original ROM supplies unrecovered material; presence of a build system does not mean the game is fully reconstructed.
Native DS/DSi adaptation of the reverse-engineered Space Cadet engine. Full Tilt CADET data is reported nonworking, and DS downscaling/light issues differ from DSi.
Hex-Rays MIPS microcode extension for selected Allegrex operations including bitrev, mfic, min/max and wsbw. mtic and instructions in delay slots remain unsupported.
ROM rework of historical GSFORTH includes subroutine-threaded Forth and block storage with readable 6502 assembly. Modern changes mean it is not an unchanged 1983 binary.
Port derived from Acornsoft Forth disassembly, retaining a 6502 host stub while running Forth on the Z80 second processor. Interactive but incomplete, with unit tests documented.
Reads WAV samples into tape streams, flags suspect bits/checksums and renders tokenized BASIC. Editing and TAP/WAV export are TODOs, despite the broader repository description.

Rosanne-native capture draws glyphs on white/black backgrounds, reads pixels and metrics, then creates BDF and pixel-outline TTF. It does not extract original scalable-font outlines. Captured fonts/OS files are not shipped.
Pocket Linker parallel-port cartridge backup/write/verify source. Current master is explicitly untested by the maintainer because suitable parallel-port hardware is unavailable.

Generates batch files, assembly and file lists to combine prepared images/audio into MACS animation. It orchestrates existing image/ADPCM/assembler/linker tools rather than implementing every converter itself.

Collection of BASIC listing converters, not a single full interpreter. Microsoft dialect testing varies; Sorcerer/Nascom/OSI variants are explicitly untested and ZBasic token maps incomplete. Top-level README describes ancestry rather than full current scope.
Unified Acorn disk/archive/BASIC toolkit with DFS/ADFS/AFS components and metadata-preserving ZIP handling. Parser resolves SparkFS, INF and filename metadata; per-filesystem operations differ.

Modern Lua/LOVE2D visual editor imitates retro aesthetics, but inspected sources do not establish native retro output or a reversing/preservation role. Do not infer native platform support from styling.

Saturn research and Jo Engine tutorial/example collection, not a separately buildable implementation in the inspected tree. Retain as a research source rather than promote a duplicate engine/tool project.
Archived package explicitly moved into rob-smallshire/oaknut. Promote the coherent canonical monorepo once; preserve old import namespace and migration relationship.
